label: D2 after a2 reaching S2 (common a2->S2), early in the episode
explanation: Fires only at D2 and essentially only when the reached state shown is S2 (99.8% of mass; S1 almost never). Within that it is mostly the common a2->S2 transition (rare a1->S2 fires weakly, ~6% of mass). It has a strong episode-time dependence: rate and magnitude are highest in the first ~10 trials and fall steadily, near zero by trial ~50 and silent after trial 60, so the GRU state drifts across an episode and this gate unit tracks that. Magnitude is also higher when the model value is high and the policy leans a2. Never fires at D1 or GO, or when reward input is 1. Reward, stay/switch and the good state matter little beyond their correlation with S2 being reached. All variables used are observed at D2 (ep_trial = elapsed time, which the agent could track implicitly).

issues: The core claims hold. Phase GO and phase D1 both score 0 activity. D2 & S1 has precision 0.002. D2 at ep_trial>=60 scores 0. D2 & S2 & a1 (rare) is weak: dev mass 0.056, test precision 0.25 even when ep_trial<40. Activity falls steadily with episode position: precision 0.99 at ep_trial 10-19, 0.61 at 30-39, 0.19 at 40-49 and 0.02 at 50-59.

Test score reproduces: P 0.878, R 0.861, F1 0.869, mass recall 0.915. The misses on the test split show no single large class. The missed mass (8.5%) is mostly rare a1->S2 steps and a2->S2 steps just past trial 40.

The claim that reward adds little is partly wrong. prev_reward (the reward input at this trial's D1, observed) changes where the episode cutoff falls. Within the predicate, precision is 0.983 when prev_reward==0 and 0.810 when prev_reward==1. Many test false positives come after a rewarded trial. Letting the cutoff depend on prev_reward raises test F1 from 0.869 to 0.897. This is a modulation of the cutoff, not a missing class of firing.
The hidden good state and start_high only weakly modulate firing within the predicate (precision about 0.81 when good==1 or start_high==1, vs 0.87 overall). They add nothing as extra conditions.
Within the predicate's support, value>0 changes nothing (identical scores), so the magnitude claim about high value is unsupported by this check. It is not tested further here.
